Skills in action

Practical examples of how I approach documentation, data quality, and process reliability.

Clinical Data Management & EDC Operations1. Source-to-eCRF Data Entry & Verification

ScenarioEntering patient data from source documents and hospital records into iMedidata and REDCap for a clinical trial.

ActionI match every entry to the source record and the protocol, and check units, dates and values for completeness and accuracy before saving, in line with ICH-GCP and ALCOA+.

OutcomeMistakes are caught at the point of entry, so fewer queries come back and the audit trail stays clean. Over 100+ source documents reviewed, this kept the data accurate, complete and consistent.

Clinical Data Management & EDC Operations2. Query & Discrepancy Resolution

ScenarioAn investigator, sponsor or site team member raises a query on an entered value, such as a visit date that does not match the record.

ActionI go back to the source record, find the cause, and reply in the EDC system with a clear, factual answer. If a correction is needed, I make it only where authorised.

OutcomeQueries close without back-and-forth, and the data stays on track for reporting deadlines.

Healthcare & Clinical Quality Assurance3. Document Control & SOP Management

ScenarioClinical and quality healthcare records spread across 30+ infertility centres need consistent versions, clear traceability and current SOPs.

ActionI manage document and version control, review records against source data, and draft or update SOPs as clinic and system requirements change, recommending workflow improvements along the way.

OutcomeRecords stay traceable and ALCOA+ compliant, and sites work from current procedures. That adds up to 500+ documents reviewed and 20+ SOPs drafted or updated.

Healthcare & Clinical Quality Assurance4. Quality Audits, RCA & CAPA

ScenarioA documentation review turns up a discrepancy or deviation, such as a gap between a record and its source.

ActionI raise it with the site and quality teams, work out the root cause, and support the corrective and preventive action. The findings go into a report for management review.

OutcomeGaps are fixed at the process level, and audit and inspection readiness improves across the sites reviewed.

Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Quality5. Batch Packaging Records & Area Logs

ScenarioRunning secondary packaging under tight production deadlines while keeping every record GMP-compliant.

ActionI complete batch and packaging records as the work happens, check that each entry is accurate and signed, keep area-specific logs up to date, and coordinate with Production, Stores and QMS.

OutcomeRecords stay accurate, traceable and inspection-ready, and dispatch operations have the documentation they need.

Professional Project: Oasis Fertility

Retrospective analysis conducted at Oasis Centre for Reproductive Medicine.

Effect of Lunar Phases on IVF Outcomes

Oasis Centre for Reproductive Medicine

A retrospective study in the infertility healthcare sector evaluating whether lunar phases have any statistical effect on IVF outcomes. The project involved deep data cleaning, abstraction of clinic records, and AI-assisted analytical reporting to provide actionable insights for the medical and statistical teams.

Data cleaningAI-assisted reportingStatistical Review
Study Details & Outcomesplan, work, resources, results

Plan

A retrospective analysis at Oasis Centre for Reproductive Medicine, set up to test whether lunar phases had any effect on IVF outcomes.

What was done

I cleaned and abstracted the available records, then prepared the graphs and analysis.

Resources and communication

I used AI-assisted reporting to present the work with the statistical team, the IT team and my manager.

Final results

The statistical review indicated no meaningful relationship; the initial apparent association was negligible and may have been coincidental.

Publication

Peer-reviewed research I co-authored on how telemedicine affects patient care.

The Impact of Telemedicine on Patient Outcomes: A Review

European Journal of Pharmaceutical and Medical Research (EJPMR). Asif Ahmed is the first and corresponding author.

Telemedicine delivers medical care remotely through digital communication. This review looks at what that means for patients: how well treatment works, how satisfied patients are, how easily they can reach care, and what it costs. It finds that telemedicine widens access, supports chronic disease management and can reduce hospital readmissions, while digital literacy, uneven technology and regulatory barriers still limit it.

TelemedicineChronic disease managementCost efficiencyHealthcarePatient outcomes

Clinical effectiveness

What the review foundworks vs gets in the way
  • Better access to healthcare
  • Improved chronic disease management
  • Fewer hospital readmissions
  • Digital literacy
  • Uneven access to technology
  • Regulatory barriers

The authors conclude that more research is needed to bring telemedicine into routine care.

Inside the papermonitoring, savings, challenges
  • Diabetes: glucose monitors and apps let clinicians spot trends and adjust care
  • Hypertension: home blood pressure readings sent to the care team
  • Heart failure: digital scales and wearables flag early warning signs
  • Fewer hospital admissions and emergency visits
  • Shorter consultations, so clinicians see more patients
  • Less travel, childcare and time off work for patients
  • Earlier detection, before treatment gets costly
  • Licensing and prescribing rules differ between regions
  • Reimbursement is inconsistent
  • Data privacy, security and informed consent need strong safeguards
  • Broadband gaps and poor links to health records
  • More research on long-term outcomes and clinician views
